basics.name: Roberto Chang-Silva
basics.summary: Ph.D. Candidate in Applied Artificial Intelligence. Research on spatiotemporal forecasting, geospatial ML pipelines, and climate modeling, with a focus on flash drought prediction.

work.name: Seoul National University of Science and Technology (AIRLab)
work.position: Ph.D. Researcher (Applied AI), under Prof. SeongYoung Park
work.summary: Developing a Transformer-based model for flash drought prediction, and a satellite-informed sensor placement algorithm for urban PM2.5 monitoring.
highlights: Transformer-based flash drought prediction that outperforms LSTM and CNN baselines across surface and root zone soil moisture.
Multi-criteria sensor placement algorithm (NSGA-II) for urban PM2.5 monitoring that reduces deployment costs while keeping near-optimal coverage.

work.name: Kyung Hee University (EMSEL Lab)
work.position: M.Sc. Researcher, under Prof. ChangKyoo Yoo
work.summary: Research on urban air quality forecasting with graph-based deep learning.
highlights: Architected LSTGraphNet, a Spatiotemporal Long Short-Term Graph Convolutional Network for urban PM2.5 forecasting, improving prediction performance by 22% over baseline models.
Reduced underestimation at high temporal horizons by 10%.
Demonstrated generalization at monitoring stations with low spatiotemporal correlation.

work.name: ESPOL Polytechnic University
work.summary: Teaching and mentoring in surveying, GIS, groundwater modeling, and mining engineering.
highlights: Designed and delivered the Surveying course from scratch for cohorts of about 30 civil and mining engineering students per semester.
Instructed courses in GIS, Groundwater Modeling (Feflow), Mine Design, and Drilling & Blasting.
Mentored undergraduate students in geospatial research, contributing to co-authored conference proceedings at LACCEI 2020 and LACCEI 2021.
